title: Cucumber, bean and dill pasta salad

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Dried pasta, olive oil, Dijon mustard, tinned cannellini beans and capers are all ordinary cupboard staples.

supermarket.reason: Every ingredient is an everyday item at Tesco or any mainstream supermarket.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a pan, a sieve, a bowl and a knife, with simple boiling and chopping.

works.reason: 300g pasta with a tin of beans, a cucumber and radishes makes a sensible lunch for four, with a well-balanced lemon and mustard dressing.

honest_times.reason: Twenty minutes is fair for deseeding and slicing the cucumber, slicing the radishes and spring onions, chopping the herbs and whisking the dressing, and twelve minutes matches the pasta boil.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning is used in the steps, nothing unlisted appears, and fusilli is a fair name for dried pasta.

seasonal_feel.reason: A cool cucumber, radish and herb pasta salad suits a mid-May lunch, and a whole cucumber is a main component rather than a garnish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are plain, clear British English that a beginner could follow.

hearty_healthy.reason: Pasta with beans, fresh vegetables and herbs makes a filling, balanced lunch a family would happily eat again.
